newsitem.title: SUDAN: Traffic accident kills 62 in Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Traffic accident kills 62 in Sudan.

text.p: Sixty-two people were killed and 30 injured when three vehicles collided on a motorway in Sudan in the country's worst road accident in a decade, Sudanese television said on Monday.

It said the accident took place on Saturday night near the town of el-Kamlin, 80 km (50 miles) southeast of Khartoum, when a van tried to overtake a truck and collided head-on with a bus coming in the opposite direction.
El-Kamlin lies on the main road linking Khartoum and Wad Medani, Sudan's second largest city.
The van and the bus were completely burned.
Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir sent State Minister for Roads and Communications Major-General Sayed Al-Husseini Abdel-Karim to el-Kamlin to pay condolences to the victims' families.
State television quoted Abdel-Karim as promising severe punishment for those responsible.
He said the van driver, who is still alive, was speeding when he tried to overtake the truck on a part of the motorway where overtaking was prohibited.
Witnesses said it took them a long time to break open the bus door and that by the time they did, most passengers had burned to death.
A police officer said the motorway was full of potholes and did not have any traffic signs.
